prerequisites: Contents of Physics and Mathematics from the university access degree.

learning_outcomes.text: Know and value the variables and processes involved in the movement and equilibrium of mechanical systems.
Understand the formulation in terms of force and moment balance that determines the state of motion or equilibrium of mechanical systems in typical engineering applications.
Understand and apply conservation principles in the analysis of mechanical situations.
Understand the nature and formulation of wave motion.
Application of knowledge to realistic situations in the field of engineering.
Ability to abstract and visualize physical phenomena.
Ability to understand the causes associated with physical processes and their consequences.
Ability to deduce the mathematical equations that describe a given physical phenomenon from physical laws and hypotheses.
Ability to understand and make approximations based on physical hypotheses.

syllabus_topics: Mathematical Foundations for Physics. Units and Physical Magnitudes. Review of Trigonometry and systems of equations. Review of differential and integral calculus. Vector algebra. Introduction to vector analysis. Physical applications.

Particle Kinematics. Trajectory, position, and displacement. Velocity and acceleration. Fundamental equations of kinematics. Kinematics in one dimension. Kinematics in two and three dimensions: composition of movements. Kinematics of circular motion.
Particle Dynamics. Newton's laws of motion and applications. Reference frames and Galileo's relativity. Friction forces. Impulse and linear momentum. Angular momentum.
Work and Energy. Work, kinetic energy, and potential energy. Kinetic energy theorem. Conservative and non-conservative forces. Potential. Conservation of mechanical energy.

Dynamics of a System of Particles. Definition of a system of particles and types. Center of mass of a system of particles. Linear momentum and conservation principle. Law of dynamics of a system of particles. Particle collisions.
Rigid Body Dynamics. Rotation. Rotation of rigid bodies. Angular momentum. Calculation of moments of inertia. Dynamics of rotational motion. Moments of force. Newton's second law for rotation.
Equilibrium and Elasticity. Forces and lines of action. Equilibrium conditions. Stress, strain, and moduli of elasticity. Elasticity and plasticity.
Periodic Motion. Simple harmonic motion. Simple pendulum and physical pendulum. Damped oscillations. Forced oscillations and resonance.
Wave Mechanics. Wave motion. Mathematical description of a wave. Sound waves. Sound intensity. Doppler effect. Elements of acoustics.
assessment_rules: Continuous evaluation includes a partial exam (topics 2-9, 10% each if passed), lab reports (10%), a practical exam (10%), and a final exam for remaining content (variable weight, max 80%). Completion of lab activities and reports is mandatory, and a minimum grade of 5/10 on the final exam is required to pass the course in continuous evaluation. For the extraordinary exam, assessment comprises an 80% theory/problem exam and a 20% lab practical grade. Students opting for unique final evaluation will be assessed by an 80% theory/problem exam, 10% lab report evaluation, and 10% lab practical exam.
